explanations.title: 他 (he) vs 她 (she)
explanations.summary: 他 and 她 sound exactly the same: tā. Only the writing tells them apart, so learn to spot the left-hand side.

explanations.title: 她 (she) vs 他 (he)
explanations.summary: 她 is tā, “she”. It sounds the same as 他 (he), but the left part is 女, “woman”.

explanations.title: 好 is built from 女 and 子
explanations.summary: 好 (hǎo, good) is a small picture made from two characters you already know: 女 (woman) and 子 (child).

explanations.title: 日 (sun / day) vs 月 (moon / month)
explanations.summary: 日 can mean sun or day; 月 can mean moon or month. Both are common, box-like characters, so compare the inner strokes.

explanations.title: 月 (moon / month) vs 日 (sun / day)
explanations.summary: 月 means moon or month, while 日 means sun or day. Both meanings appear often in beginner Chinese.

explanations.title: 人 (person) and 大 (big)
explanations.summary: 人 means person. 大 means big. Their shapes are related-looking, but 大 has an extra stroke across the upper body.

explanations.title: 大 (big) and 人 (person)
explanations.summary: 大 means big; 人 means person. The added horizontal stroke is the quickest way to tell 大 apart from 人.

explanations.title: 一 (one) and its tone changes
explanations.summary: 一 is yī when said alone, but its tone commonly changes in connected speech. These are pronunciation changes, not different characters.

explanations.title: 不 (bù) changes before a fourth tone
explanations.summary: 不 means not. It is usually bù alone, but becomes bú before a following fourth-tone syllable in ordinary speech.

explanations.title: 木 (wood / tree) and 目 (eye)
explanations.summary: 木 and 目 are both pronounced mù, but they mean different things. Look at the shape and the meaning rather than the sound alone.

explanations.title: 十 (ten) and 石 (stone)
explanations.summary: 十 means ten and 石 means stone. They are pronounced the same in Mandarin (shí), so the sound alone cannot distinguish them.

explanations.title: 石 (stone) and 十 (ten)
explanations.summary: 石 means stone and 十 means ten. Both are shí, so they are homophones: the pronunciation is the same.

explanations.title: 女 (woman) appears in other characters
explanations.summary: 女 means woman or female. You have already seen it as the left-hand part of 她 and as one part of 好.

explanations.title: 子 (child) appears in 好
explanations.summary: 子 means child and is one of the parts in 好 (hǎo, good). The association can help you remember the character.

explanations.title: 上 (above) and 下 (below)
explanations.summary: 上 means above or up; 下 means below or down. Their meanings are opposites and their short strokes sit on opposite sides of a long horizontal line.

explanations.title: 下 (below) and 上 (above)
explanations.summary: 下 means below or down, the opposite of 上 (above or up). Check where the short stroke sits relative to the long line.

explanations.title: 马 (horse)
explanations.summary: 马 means horse. Its shape is distinctive, and it is a useful early character to recognise.

explanations.title: 目 (eye) and 木 (wood)
explanations.summary: 目 means eye and is pronounced mù, just like 木 (wood / tree). The extra inner lines help distinguish the written forms.

explanations.title: 你好 (hello)
explanations.summary: 你好 is the basic greeting. Both syllables are third tone, and in speech the first one is usually said with a rising tone.

explanations.title: 谢谢 (thank you)
explanations.summary: 谢谢 is how you say thank you. The second syllable is neutral tone, so it is short and light.

explanations.title: 朋友 (friend)
explanations.summary: 朋友 has a neutral second syllable: péngyou. The 友 is short and light, and pinyin shows this by leaving off the tone mark.

explanations.title: 今天 (today)
explanations.summary: 今天 means today. Both syllables are first tone, high and level.

explanations.title: 学校 (school)
explanations.summary: 学校 is a two-character word for school. Learn it as one word: you do not need to add up the meanings of 学 and 校.

explanations.title: 喜欢 (to like)
explanations.summary: 喜欢 means to like. The second syllable is neutral tone: xǐhuan.

explanations.title: 妈妈 (mom)
explanations.summary: 妈妈 is mā-ma: the second syllable is neutral tone. Many family words repeat a character this way.

explanations.title: 谁 (who): shéi or shuí
explanations.summary: Two pronunciations are both correct for 谁: shéi and shuí. They are the same word with the same meaning, so a question never counts one of them as wrong.

explanations.title: 看 (kàn): to look / watch
explanations.summary: 看 has two readings with different meanings. kàn (fourth tone) is the common one: to look, watch or read. Do not mix it up with kān, which means to guard.

explanations.title: 看 (kān): to guard
explanations.summary: kān (first tone) means to guard or look after. It is much rarer than kàn. The character is the same, only the reading and meaning differ.

explanations.title: 吗 (question particle)
explanations.summary: 吗 is not translated. Put it at the end of a statement to turn it into a yes/no question. It is always neutral tone.

explanations.title: 的 (links a describing word to a noun)
explanations.summary: 的 has no single English word. It joins something that describes a noun to that noun: 我的书 is my book.

explanations.title: 了 (finished action or new situation)
explanations.summary: 了 has no single English word. After a verb it often shows that the action is done; at the end of a sentence it can show a change. Here it is read le (neutral tone).
